prompt: Traffic averages 310/s and its busiest hour runs at 3 times that. Your app server keeps up, and your code makes 4 queries for every request it serves. How many queries per second reach the database at peak?

options.whyWrong: This is the request rate, not the query rate. Each request the app server serves makes several queries, and every one of them is load on the database.
This works the load out at the weekly mean. The game resolves each week at its busiest hour, so the database has to carry the peak rate of queries.
This is the average request rate. It misses both the busy hour and the queries each request makes, so it understates the database’s load twice over.

explanation: At peak the app server receives 310 × 3 = 930/s and serves all of it. Each served request makes 4 queries, so the database receives 930 × 4 = 3,720/s. Load is always worked out at the busiest hour.

prompt: At peak, your app server’s p99 is 150 ms and your database’s is 20 ms. Every request passes through both. What p99 does this game report for the whole path?

options.whyWrong: This is the app server’s figure alone. A request also waits at the database, and this game adds each hop’s p99 into the path’s.
This averages the two hops. A request crosses both, so their times add rather than average; percentiles never average in this game.
This is the database’s figure alone, as if a request’s time were decided where its path ends. Every hop it crossed on the way counts too.

explanation: This game adds up each hop’s p99 along the path: 150 + 20 = 170 ms. Real tails rarely line up on the same request, so the true figure is lower, but the sum is what the game judges you on, and it makes every hop count.
